title: Advanced Causal and Consecutive Linking
summary: Expressing causes, reasons, consequences, and resulting conditions across sentence structures.
whyItMatters: Varied causal and consecutive structures clarify whether a phrase introduces evidence, a reason, a mechanism, or a consequence.

mentalModel.title: Cause points backward; consequence points forward
mentalModel.content: Causal connectors explain why something happens, while consecutive connectors state what follows.

mentalModel.title: Connector type controls word order
mentalModel.content: Subordinating conjunctions, coordinating adverbs, and prepositions create different sentence patterns.

ruleBlocks.title: Choose causal structures
ruleBlocks.content: Use weil, da, zumal, dadurch dass, aufgrund plus genitive, or wegen plus genitive/dative according to register and emphasis.

ruleBlocks.title: Choose consecutive structures
ruleBlocks.content: Use sodass/so dass, weshalb, daher, folglich, infolgedessen, or infolge plus genitive.

ruleBlocks.title: Avoid claiming unsupported causation
ruleBlocks.content: Use beitragen zu, zusammenhängen mit, or begünstigen when evidence shows influence rather than a single proven cause.

examples.de: Da Erholungsphasen fehlen, kann sich die Belastung verstärken.
examples.en: Because recovery phases are absent, the strain can intensify.

examples.de: Klare Zuständigkeiten tragen dazu bei, dass Konflikte früher gelöst werden.
examples.en: Clear responsibilities help conflicts be resolved earlier.

examples.de: Die Wartezeit war sehr lang, sodass viele Betroffene keine rechtzeitige Unterstützung erhielten.
examples.en: The waiting time was very long, so many affected people did not receive timely support.

commonMistakes.wrong: Place the finite verb directly after weil.
commonMistakes.correct: Put the finite verb at the end of the subordinate clause.
commonMistakes.reason: Weil is a subordinating conjunction in standard written German.

commonMistakes.wrong: Use verursacht when evidence shows only association.
commonMistakes.reason: Grammar should reflect the strength of the evidence.

comparisons.summary: Health contexts require multi-causal explanations and careful claims.
Advice becomes clearer when reasons and likely consequences are explicitly linked.
